# lsed

[![lsed package hexagonal
logo](reference/figures/logo.png)](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/)

A software package (R and Python) for determining the benefit of using a
statistical model in landscape decision making. Currently using minor
extensions of decision curve analysis (DCA), geared towards species
distribution models.

## Overview

boop boop.

## Installation

lsed is available only on github, with plans for submission to CRAN. It
can be installed using `remotes` or `devtools` (or `pak` etc.):

``` r

install.packages('remotes')
remotes::install_github('sagesteppe/lsed')
```

## Functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----|----|
| [`reweight()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/reweight.md) | Case weights that re-price an evaluation sample to a target prevalence |
| [`roc_auc()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/roc_auc.md) | Prevalence-invariant ROC-AUC via the rank (Mann-Whitney) identity |
| [`ap_pointwise()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/ap_pointwise.md), [`pr_curve_exact()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/pr_curve_exact.md) | Exact average precision / PR curve at a target prevalence |
| [`ap_binormal()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/ap_binormal.md), [`pr_curve_binormal()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/pr_curve_binormal.md), [`ap_scalar_to_prev()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/ap_scalar_to_prev.md) | Equal-variance binormal (summary-metric) route |
| [`nb_exact()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_exact.md), [`nb_binormal()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_binormal.md), [`nb_treat_all()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_treat_all.md) | Decision-curve net benefit (per-point, best-achievable, treat-all) |
| [`cox_calibration()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/cox_calibration.md), [`recalibrate_to_prevalence()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/recalibrate_to_prevalence.md), [`clamp()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/clamp.md) | Calibration helpers |
| [`survey_units()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/survey_units.md) | Convert a continuous raster into survey units |

# Package index

## Prevalence weighting

Re-price an evaluation sample to a target landscape prevalence.

- [`reweight()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/reweight.md)
  : Prevalence case weights

## Reported diagnostics

The two per-sample summary scores a model reports. ROC-AUC is
prevalence-invariant but inflated by easy absences; PR-AUC is the
recommended anchor for curve reconstruction.

- [`roc_auc()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/roc_auc.md)
  : ROC-AUC via the rank (Mann-Whitney) identity
- [`pr_auc()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/pr_auc.md) :
  Reported precision-recall AUC (average precision) at the sample
  prevalence

## Average precision & PR curves

Precision-recall at a target prevalence, by the exact point-level route
and the equal-variance binormal (summary-metric) route.

- [`ap_pointwise()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/ap_pointwise.md)
  : Exact per-point average precision (PR-AUC) at a target prevalence
- [`ap_binormal()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/ap_binormal.md)
  : Average precision of an equal-variance binormal ROC at a prevalence
- [`ap_scalar_to_prev()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/ap_scalar_to_prev.md)
  : Correct a scalar PR-AUC from its design prevalence to a target
  prevalence
- [`pr_curve_exact()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/pr_curve_exact.md)
  : Exact precision-recall curve at a target prevalence
- [`pr_curve_binormal()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/pr_curve_binormal.md)
  : Reconstructed precision-recall curve from a binormal ROC at a
  prevalence

## Net benefit (decision curves)

Decision-curve net benefit and its reference strategies.

- [`nb_exact()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_exact.md)
  : Net benefit of thresholded predictions at a target prevalence
- [`nb_exact_ci()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_exact_ci.md)
  : Bootstrap confidence band for the exact net-benefit curve
- [`nb_binormal()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_binormal.md)
  : Best-achievable net benefit from an equal-variance binormal ROC
- [`nb_binormal_band()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_binormal_band.md)
  : Plausibility band for a binormal net-benefit curve from PR-AUC
  uncertainty
- [`nb_treat_all()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/nb_treat_all.md)
  : Net benefit of the treat-all (survey-everything) reference strategy

## Calibration

Assess and shift the calibration of held-out predictions.

- [`cox_calibration()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/cox_calibration.md)
  : Cox calibration intercept and slope on held-out predictions
- [`recalibrate_to_prevalence()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/recalibrate_to_prevalence.md)
  : Recalibrate predicted probabilities to a target prevalence (logit
  shift)
- [`clamp()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/clamp.md) :
  Clamp probabilities away from 0 and 1

## Survey-unit delineation

Turn a predicted suitability surface into mapped survey units end to end
(watershed patches, subdivided and attributed). The low-level stages are
internal; this is the single entry point.

- [`survey_units()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/survey_units.md)
  : Delineate survey units end to end

## Patch ranking (RankIndex)

Prioritise candidate patches by combining rescaled terms. The network
engine routes travel on roads/trails to score accessibility (A) and, on
the same graph, complementarity (C) — whether a day’s work can be
assembled nearby.

- [`rank_index()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/rank_index.md)
  : Combine the RankIndex terms into a priority score

- [`network`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/network.md) :
  Accessibility (A) and complementarity (C) on a road/trail network
  graph

- [`accessibility()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/accessibility.md)
  : Accessibility of patches over the network (A)

- [`complementarity()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/complementarity.md)
  : Complementarity of patches: can a day's work be assembled nearby?
  (C)

- [`contract_network()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/contract_network.md)
  : Contract an OSM network to junction-to-junction edges

- [`osm_speeds`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/osm_speeds.md)
  :

  Default per-`highway` travel speeds (km/h)

## RankIndex — distance terms (Dg, Dr, A)

Isotropic, terra-native distance surfaces: straight-line distance from
known populations (Dg), least-cost resistance distance (Dr) over a
friction surface, and Tobler walking cost for accessibility.

- [`cost`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/cost.md) :
  Dispersal and accessibility terms (Dg, Dr, A) by isotropic cost
  distance
- [`geo_distance()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/geo_distance.md)
  : Geographic distance from known populations (Dg)
- [`cost_distance()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/cost_distance.md)
  : Resistance / accessibility distance by isotropic cost distance (Dr,
  A)
- [`build_resistance()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/build_resistance.md)
  : Build an isotropic resistance (friction) surface
- [`tobler_friction()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/tobler_friction.md)
  : Tobler walking-cost friction for accessibility (A)
- [`cluster_region_extents()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/cluster_region_extents.md)
  : Cluster sources into buffered, cell-capped regions for tiled cost
  distance

## RankIndex — survey intensity (S)

The survey-effort “bias surface” as a gridless Gaussian field of
target-group occurrences, with inverse-frequency species weighting
corrected for domain clipping; inverted it gives survey sparsity, where
undocumented populations may hide.

- [`survey`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/survey.md) :

  Survey-intensity surface (the `S` term) as a continuous Gaussian field

- [`survey_surface()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/survey_surface.md)
  : Build the survey-intensity surface in one call

- [`survey_weights()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/survey_weights.md)
  : Inverse-frequency species weights, corrected for domain clipping

- [`guess_record_type()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/guess_record_type.md)
  : Guess record type from a dataset / origin column

## RankIndex — pipeline modules

The two halves of a run: acquire every external input once (download),
then compute all terms and combine them (calculate). Split so the slow,
API-bound acquisition is reused while weights are tuned.

- [`rank_download()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/rank_download.md)
  : Acquire every external input for the patch ranking (download module)
- [`rank_calculate()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/rank_calculate.md)
  : Score patches from the downloaded inputs (calculate module)

## Data acquisition (GBIF & OSM)

Fetch the external inputs — target-group occurrences from GBIF’s bulk
download (for S) and the OSM road/trail network scoped to patch clusters
(for A/C). Both cache to disk; be a good API citizen.

- [`gbif_records()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/gbif_records.md)
  : Fetch target-group occurrence records from GBIF for the
  survey-intensity term
- [`gbif_request()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/gbif_request.md)
  : Request a GBIF download (non-blocking) - stage 1 of 2
- [`gbif_retrieve()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/gbif_retrieve.md)
  : Retrieve a requested GBIF download - stage 2 of 2
- [`osm_network_for()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/osm_network_for.md)
  : Fetch an OSM network scoped to patch clusters, connected to an
  origin
- [`osm_access()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/osm_access.md)
  : Fetch the OSM access network (roads + trails) for a domain
- [`cluster_patches()`](https://sagesteppe.github.io/lsed/reference/cluster_patches.md)
  : Cluster patches into spatial groups
